Meeting header: 2026-01-17 15:00 PST | Duration 43m | Redwood: Maria Chen (AE), Liam O'Connor (SE) | Elysian Health: Dr. Priya Rao, Samir Patel, Jasmine Lee

[00:00] Maria: hey everyone, thanks for joining. um quick agenda — retainer uplift, region activation (eu/apac), and any security asks. is that good?
[00:08] Priya: yep that's perfect. we've got about 40 minutes. trying to keep it focused.
[00:13] Samir: also we need to understand the network layout for the private deployment, like peering, firewalls, and VPC stuff.
[00:20] Liam: absolutely, i'll go deep on the network and latency bits. maria i'll kick off price and timeline.
[00:25] Maria: cool. so high level, you're proposing a phased uplift to the retainer — starting with a 2x baseline for triage traffic and then adding burst capacity for seasonal peaks, correct?
[00:34] Priya: yes. our new front-end triage introduced in prod next month will push steady QPS up by ~2x and occasional spikes to 5x for short periods.
[00:42] Maria: got it. we can offer a tiered uplift: committed baseline increase plus a burst pool billed at X/hour. i'll detail it in the quote.
[00:49] Priya: and region-wise, we need EU for residency and latency for EU users, and APAC for our Singapore and Seoul clusters. timeline is month-to-month but we'd like EU online in feb/mar and APAC by april if possible.
[01:05] Liam: quick clarifying q — when you say APAC, is the primary latency target for Singapore only or do you need multiple zones?
[01:11] Samir: primarily Singapore for now. later we'll evaluate Seoul. initial ask is <120ms p95 for SG -> inference.
[01:19] Liam: okay p95 <120ms is doable with edge zones and private nodes; depends on model size and quantization. we should run a benchmark with your sample payloads to validate.
[01:28] Priya: yes we'll provide payloads. also, do you support auto-fallback to hosted models if private capacity is saturated? last time we had a small outage and fallback would have helped.
[01:37] Maria: yes we have smart routing and fallback policies. for Dedicated/Private we can config a controlled fallback to a hosted variant; it is opt-in and we can expose the policies.
[01:46] Jasmine: from security: SOC two scope — we need to ensure logs and KMS usage are auditable, and we need a contract clause about data residency for EU tenants. is that in your standard enterprise package?
[01:56] Maria: we include audit logs and KMS integration options; SOC2 artifact pack is in our security docs. i will attach the SOC two pack and our data residency playbook. any specific wording you need?
[02:07] Jasmine: we may ask for a clause that data for EU tenants remains in EU unless otherwise authorized. also, SSO/SAML integration timelines — we need SAML for our internal teams.
[02:18] Liam: SAML/SSO is supported. for private deployments, SSO can be configured during onboarding; we'll send a checklist. it typically takes a week from when you provide IdP details.
[02:26] Samir: network wise, can you outline peering vs transit options? our infra team prefers direct VPC peering but some franc — sorry, some regions only support transit.
[02:36] Liam: yes, we support both. we'll share a diagram with peering, transit, and VPN as fallbacks. note that peering gives lower latency but requires cross-account peering config — we'll document the steps.
[02:47] Maria: back to pricing — we can do a phased 2x baseline commit for 6 months, with a burst pool and a discounted rate for committed additional capacity. then reevaluate at renewal. i'll include a couple of scenarios in the quote.
[02:59] Priya: good. and for the benchmark — what metrics do you need? p95, p99, tokens per second?
[03:07] Liam: primary: p50/p95/p99 latency, throughput (tokens/sec or requests/sec), and GPU utilization. also KV cache hit rates if you're using prefix caching. send sample payloads and sequence lengths and we'll run a small synthetic run.
[03:20] Priya: ok we'll package a representative sample set.
[03:23] Jasmine: also, on audit logs — does the console expose per-token usage and per-route breakdown? we need that for chargeback.
[03:31] Maria: yes console has token-level cost and latency breakdowns per API key/route. we can also ship a weekly CSV export.
[03:38] Samir: one concern: cold start latency for larger models in APAC edge — how do you mitigate?
[03:44] Liam: we use pinned warm instances for critical routes and a smaller cold pool for less critical. plus KV caching and continuous batching to reduce token latency. for APAC we recommend at least a small dedicated pool for the first month to stabilize.
[03:58] Priya: and SLA? we will need a 99.9% uptime for the dedicated nodes.
[04:04] Maria: our Dedicated/Private tiers come with SLA options. i'll put the SLA language and the escalation path in the docs.
[04:10] Jasmine: final question — any vendor lock or long-term migration constraints?
[04:14] Maria: no lock-in; you can pin model versions and migrate. for private we provide tooling to export model artifacts and cache states on request.
[04:22] Priya: great. let's recap next steps.
[04:25] Maria: recap: i'll send updated quote with phased uplift and burst pricing by Jan 20; liam will share VPC checklist and network diagram by Jan 19; samir will provide sample payloads and peak QPS by Jan 24; jasmine will confirm SOC two scope and any contract language by Jan 22. we'll propose two slots for onboarding kickoff (pilot) for Jan 27.
[04:45] Samir: that sounds right. thanks all.
[04:48] Priya: thanks, bye.
